two-top/e06cf2a:
Two reports: the web version differs from the APK "in ways", and the
controls did not work in Android Chrome. The second is mine — last
batch made the touch controls visible without checking that anything
consumed them, so they rendered, tracked the thumb, and fed nothing.
That is worse than the bug it replaced, because it looks like a broken
game rather than a missing feature.

One habit caused all of it: `#[cfg(not(target_os = "android"))]` was
used to mean "desktop". It means "desktop AND the browser", and the
browser build is mostly opened on a phone.

D1 (critical) — touch never reached the simulation.
`read_android_touch_inputs` is the ONLY thing anywhere that turns
`TouchState` into `LocalInputs`, and it is Android-gated; the
not(android) arm installs the keyboard plugin. So the wasm build had no
input source at all on a device with no keyboard. `InputTouchPlugin`
runs everywhere and kept `TouchState` current, which is exactly why the
stick animated under the thumb while the duelist stood still. Fixed by
LAYERING a browser touch source over the keyboard one rather than
choosing between them: one wasm binary serves a phone and a laptop.
`read_web_touch_inputs` writes only while a finger is engaged
(`input_touch::is_engaged`, including the sticky-release latch that
carries an aimed throw), so a laptop browser keeps WASD and couch
versus. It mirrors for the flipped P1 client itself, like the Android
reader, and runs after `mirror_desktop_inputs_for_flip` so the
reflection lands once, not twice.

D2 — the browser paid a desktop's render cost. The camera's cheap path
(LDR, no bloom, no MSAA) was Android-only; the browser took HDR +
Bloom::OLD_SCHOOL. The Android comment measures what that costs: ~65
ms/frame for the HDR+bloom chain and ~17 for MSAA, pinning a Galaxy A16
at 10 fps — and the web build asked for it through WebGL2, a worse
place to request an HDR target than native GLES ever was. The cheap
path is now any(android, wasm).

D3 — riding in that same bloc
